content.title: About
content.content: Red potatoes without skin are fresh tubers that have had their skins removed, revealing a creamy white flesh. They have a mild, slightly sweet flavor and a firm, creamy texture when cooked. Raw red potatoes are often used in salads, marinades, and dishes where color and nutrients need to be preserved.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Red potatoes contain more antioxidants than white varieties thanks to anthocyanins in the skin, some of which remain after peeling.
Raw potatoes are a good source of vitamin C, which is largely destroyed by heat.
In many regions red potatoes are grown in cooler climates where they hold their shape better.
Peeling accelerates nutrient loss, so it’s best to prepare them soon after cleaning.
Red potatoes are sometimes used in traditional dishes like Russian “Olivier” salad to add a splash of color.

items.title: Rich in vitamin C
items.content: Vitamin C supports the immune system and aids collagen synthesis.

items.title: Source of potassium
items.content: Potassium helps regulate blood pressure and muscle function.

items.title: Contains dietary fiber
items.content: Fiber promotes healthy digestion and a feeling of fullness.

items.title: Antioxidant content
items.content: Anthocyanins and other phytochemicals protect cells from oxidative stress.

items.title: Low in fat
items.content: Potatoes contain virtually no fat, making them suitable for balanced diets.

items.title: Solanine content
items.content: Raw potatoes may contain solanine, a toxin that concentrates in green spots and sprouts. Do not eat green or sprouted parts.

items.title: Allergy
items.content: Some individuals may experience an allergic reaction to potatoes.

items.title: High glycemic index
items.content: Potatoes can raise blood sugar quickly, so people with diabetes should monitor portions.

items.title: Foodborne risk if stored improperly
items.content: Storing at warm temperatures can allow growth of Clostridium botulinum.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Raw red potatoes can be thinly sliced for salads, pickled in vinegar, added to cold appetizers, or used as a base for vegetable chips. They should be washed thoroughly and, if desired, briefly blanched to reduce solanine levels before consumption.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep peeled red potatoes in the refrigerator in an airtight container lined with a damp cloth for 2‑3 days. For longer storage, keep them in a cool, dark place with the skin on and peel just before use.
